_comment: Prompt Guru tool syntax rules. Each entry defines how the final prompt must be formatted for that tool. Edit this file to tune output or add tools — no Worker code changes needed. The Worker fetches this from the live site at /prompt_formats.json.

midjourney.label: Midjourney
midjourney.style: comma-separated descriptive phrases with parameter flags
rules: Comma-separated descriptive phrases, not full sentences
Order: subject first, then style, then lighting/mood, then composition
End with parameter flags: aspect ratio as --ar W:H, version as --v 6
If the user wants to avoid something, use --no <thing> flag
Keep under 350 characters before flags
midjourney.example: golden retriever astronaut floating inside a space station, photorealistic, warm rim lighting, shallow depth of field, shot on 85mm lens --ar 16:9 --v 6

dalle.label: DALL-E
rules: Write as one or two natural, flowing sentences
No flags, no parameter syntax, no tag lists
Be explicit about style (e.g. 'a photorealistic photo of', 'a watercolor illustration of')
State composition and lighting in plain language
Mention what to avoid in plain words if needed
dalle.example: A photorealistic photo of a golden retriever wearing a NASA spacesuit floating inside a space station, warm light from a window, gentle and playful mood, centered composition.

stable-diffusion.label: Stable Diffusion
stable-diffusion.style: tag-style prompt plus separate negative prompt
rules: Main prompt: comma-separated tags and short phrases, most important first
Include quality tags like 'highly detailed, sharp focus' where appropriate
Always provide a separate 'Negative prompt:' line listing what to avoid
No sentence structure needed — density of relevant tags matters more
Keep main prompt under 300 characters
stable-diffusion.example:
golden retriever in astronaut suit, space station interior, photorealistic, highly detailed, warm lighting, sharp focus, 85mm
Negative prompt: blurry, cartoon, extra limbs, text, watermark

ideogram.label: Ideogram
ideogram.style: natural sentences, strong at rendering text in images
rules: Natural descriptive sentences
If the image should contain visible text, put the exact text in double quotes
State the style plainly (poster, logo, photo, illustration)
Mention color palette if the user expressed one
ideogram.example: A retro travel poster of a space station with the text "GREETINGS FROM ORBIT" in bold vintage lettering, warm sunset palette, clean vector illustration style.

adobe-firefly.label: Adobe Firefly
rules: Write as one or two clear, natural sentences
No flags or tag syntax — Firefly reads plain descriptive language
Firefly favors clean commercial/editorial imagery — lean toward polished, brand-safe phrasing
State style, lighting, and composition explicitly in plain words
Mention if a transparent background or specific aspect ratio is needed
adobe-firefly.example: A clean product photo of a golden retriever wearing a small astronaut helmet, studio lighting, white background, commercial photography style.

krea.label: Krea
rules: Krea is used for real-time generation — keep prompts short and punchy, not long paragraphs
Lead with the single most important visual element
Comma-separated style descriptors work well, similar to Midjourney but no flags needed
Keep under 200 characters — short prompts iterate better in real-time tools
krea.example: golden retriever astronaut, space station, photorealistic, warm lighting, detailed

leonardo-ai.label: Leonardo AI
leonardo-ai.style: descriptive tag-style prompt, game-art and concept-art friendly
rules: Comma-separated descriptive phrases, similar density to Stable Diffusion
Leonardo is strong at game/concept art — mention art style explicitly if relevant (concept art, character sheet, environment art)
Include lighting and material detail where relevant
Keep under 300 characters
leonardo-ai.example: golden retriever astronaut character design, concept art, space station background, dramatic rim lighting, highly detailed, digital painting

flux.label: Flux
flux.style: natural descriptive sentences with strong detail
rules: Write as flowing natural-language sentences, not tag lists
Flux responds well to specific, concrete detail — avoid vague adjectives
Describe lighting, texture, and camera/lens detail explicitly if relevant
No flags needed
flux.example: A photorealistic image of a golden retriever wearing a detailed NASA spacesuit, floating inside a softly lit space station interior, shot on an 85mm lens with shallow depth of field.

canva-ai.label: Canva AI
rules: Keep it to one simple, plain sentence — Canva's generator favors simplicity over dense detail
State the subject and style clearly
Avoid technical photography/camera jargon — plain descriptive words work best here
canva-ai.example: A cute golden retriever dressed as an astronaut, floating in a space station, colorful and friendly illustration style.

sora.label: Sora
rules: One flowing cinematic paragraph, no flags or tags
Describe the scene, then the motion, then the camera behavior
Use concrete camera language: 'slow dolly in', 'static wide shot', 'handheld tracking shot'
Describe lighting and atmosphere explicitly
Keep under 600 characters
sora.example: Gentle ocean waves rolling onto an empty beach at golden hour, warm sunlight glinting off the water. Static wide shot, slow rhythmic motion, calm meditative atmosphere with soft ambient haze.

runway.label: Runway
runway.style: concise cinematic description with explicit motion
rules: One short paragraph, motion-focused — Runway responds strongly to movement verbs
Name the camera move explicitly ('slow pan left', 'aerial pullback', 'locked-off shot')
Describe subject motion separately from camera motion
No negative prompts — not supported
Keep under 450 characters
runway.example: Slow aerial pullback over calm ocean waves at sunset, waves rolling gently toward shore, warm golden light, soft atmospheric haze, smooth continuous camera motion.

kling.label: Kling AI
kling.style: detailed scene description with physical realism cues
rules: Describe the scene in natural sentences with strong physical detail
Kling excels at realistic physics — describe how things move and interact
Specify shot type and duration feel (brief clip vs continuous take)
State the mood and lighting
kling.example: A close-up of ocean waves curling and breaking in slow motion at sunset, water droplets catching golden light, realistic fluid physics, cinematic shallow depth of field, serene mood.

pika.label: Pika
pika.style: short punchy description with style modifiers
rules: Short and direct — one or two sentences
Lead with the subject and action
Add style modifiers at the end (cinematic, anime, 3D render, claymation)
Mention camera motion simply if needed ('camera slowly zooms in')
pika.example: Ocean waves rolling onto a beach at sunset, camera slowly pans across the water, cinematic, warm tones, peaceful.

heygen.label: HeyGen
heygen.style: avatar + script instructions, not scene description
rules: HeyGen generates avatar-presenter videos, not freeform scenes — the 'prompt' is really the script the avatar will speak plus delivery notes
Write the actual spoken script as natural sentences
Add a short delivery note in brackets if tone matters, e.g. [warm, conversational tone]
Do not describe camera movement or scenery — HeyGen controls that separately
heygen.example: [Warm, conversational tone] Hi there! Ever wondered what it's like to work in zero gravity? Let me walk you through a day in the life aboard the space station.

synthesia.label: Synthesia
synthesia.style: avatar + script instructions, not scene description
rules: Like HeyGen, Synthesia's input is a spoken script for an avatar, not a visual scene description
Write natural, presenter-style sentences meant to be read aloud
Keep sentences short — avatars read more naturally with simple sentence structure
Add a short tone/delivery note in brackets if relevant
synthesia.example: [Friendly, upbeat tone] Welcome aboard! Today we're taking a look at how astronauts train before their very first mission to space.

v0.label: v0 (Vercel)
rules: Describe the UI as structured requirements: what the page/app is, then each section in order
Name concrete components (navbar, hero, pricing cards, footer) rather than vague vibes
State the visual style explicitly (minimal, glassmorphism, brutalist, corporate) and color direction
Mention responsive behavior if it matters
v0 builds React + Tailwind — you can reference shadcn/ui components by name
v0.example: A landing page for a meditation app. Sticky navbar with logo and two links. Hero with a calming gradient background, app screenshot, headline, and App Store buttons. Below: three feature cards with icons, a testimonial carousel, and a simple footer. Minimal style, soft blues and sand tones, rounded corners, generous whitespace. Fully responsive.

bolt.label: Bolt
bolt.style: full app description with tech expectations
rules: Describe the whole app: purpose, pages, and key functionality — Bolt scaffolds full projects, not just one screen
List the pages/routes you need and what each does
State data behavior plainly (what gets saved, what's just visual)
Mention the stack only if you care (otherwise Bolt picks)
Keep it organized — short paragraphs or a numbered list of requirements work well
bolt.example: Build a recipe-sharing web app. Pages: home feed of recipe cards, a recipe detail page, and a submit-recipe form (title, ingredients, steps, photo URL). Save submissions to local storage. Clean modern design, warm color palette, mobile friendly.

lovable.label: Lovable
rules: Describe it like a product brief: who it's for and what it does, then the screens
Lovable responds well to user-flow language: 'when a user clicks X, Y happens'
State the design mood in a few words (playful, corporate, elegant)
List must-have features explicitly — implied features get skipped
lovable.example: A simple habit tracker for busy professionals. Home screen shows today's habits as tappable cards that toggle done/undone, with a weekly progress bar on top. An add-habit screen with name, frequency, and reminder time. When a user completes all habits, show a small celebration animation. Clean, elegant, calming green palette.

suno.label: Suno
rules: Style prompt: comma-separated genre and mood tags (e.g. 'lo-fi hip hop, chill, mellow piano, vinyl crackle')
Include tempo/energy words (slow, driving, upbeat) and key instruments
If lyrics matter, structure them with [Verse], [Chorus], [Bridge] tags on their own lines
For instrumental tracks, just say 'instrumental' in the style
Keep the style line under 120 characters — Suno truncates long style prompts
suno.example: Style: dreamy synthwave, nostalgic, mid-tempo, analog synths, soft drums, instrumental

udio.label: Udio
udio.style: descriptive genre tags with production detail
rules: Comma-separated genre, mood, and production descriptors
Udio responds well to production language: 'warm analog mix', 'punchy drums', 'wide stereo'
Name era or artist-style influences generically ('80s synth-pop style') — not specific artist names
State vocal type if wanted (male vocals, female vocals, choir) or 'instrumental'
udio.example: uplifting orchestral cinematic, sweeping strings, powerful brass, epic percussion, warm mix, instrumental
